summary: David L. Gosling is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He held a Spalding Fellowship at Clare Hall, Cambridge, in 1992 and had an attested post at the University of Cambridge in 2001.

David L. Haberman is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Colorado from around 1970 to 1974. He held posts at the University of Arizona (~1989–1993) and Indiana University (circa 1993).

David L. McMahan works in Buddhist and religious studies. He taught at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and the University of Vermont, and served as Assistant Professor (attested 2002) and Professor of Religious Studies (attested 2013) at Franklin & Marshall College.

David Llewellyn Snellgrove was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Southampton and Cambridge, including under D. R. Shackleton Bailey, Harold Walter Bailey, and Walter Simon, and served as a professor at SOAS, University of London (1950–1982).

Historian and Indologist David Ludden studied at Yale and the University of Pennsylvania. He held posts at the University of Virginia (1979–1980), University of Pennsylvania (1981–2008), BRAC University (2005), and New York University (from 2007).

David M. DiValerio specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the School for International Training and the University of Virginia under Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee in 2015.

David M. Knipe is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who held a long career as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he also served as Chair of Religious Studies (attested between 1975 and 2001).
David Matsumoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He served as Director at the Institute of Buddhist Studies, with his posts there attested in 2004 and 2013.
David N. Keightley was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He was a professor at the University of California, Berkeley, where his posts are attested in 1985 and 1999.

David N. Lorenzen specializes in Indology, history, and religious studies. He studied at Wesleyan, SOAS, and the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, and served as a professor at El Colegio de México from 1970 to 2010.

David Ownby is a scholar of sinology, history, and religious studies. He earned his BA at Vanderbilt and PhD at Harvard, taught at Southern Methodist University (~1989–1993), and served as Professor of History at Université de Montréal (1994–2023).

David P. Chandler is a historian who studied at Harvard College, Harvard University, Yale, and the University of Michigan. He held posts at Johns Hopkins, Cornell, Wisconsin-Madison, and Monash University (~1972–1997).

David P. Jackson is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his degrees at the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg. He taught at Osaka University (1984–1986) and was a professor at the University of Hamburg (1992–2007).
David Patt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, completing his PhD under the supervision of Geshe Lhundub Sopa, attested in 1993.

David Pingree specialized in Indology and history. He completed his BA and PhD at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and Otto Neugebauer, later holding professorships at the University of Chicago (1963–1971) and Brown University (appointed 1971).

David R. Kinsley was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Drew University, Union Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago. He held a faculty post at McMaster University from 1969 to 2000.

David R. Loy is a philosopher and religious studies scholar educated at Carleton, King's College London, Hawaiʻi, and the National University of Singapore. He held posts at NUS (1978–1984), Bunkyo University (1990–2006), and Xavier University (~2006–2010).

David Ralph Quinter works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He completed an MA at Colorado and a PhD at Stanford under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, later becoming an associate professor at the University of Alberta (attested 2019).
David Ruddell was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Laval University and served as Secretary at Fort William College.

David Schaberg is a Sinologist who studied at Stanford and Harvard. He joined the University of California, Los Angeles in 1996, later serving as Dean of Humanities (2012) and Senior Dean of the College (2020).
